change: take the CED citations out of five quiz stems, so the last two held-back cyber quizzes can be server-scored
_context: 22 of 25 cyber quiz pages are now server-scored. Three still ship their own
answer key, and two of the three are held back by the SAME refusal:
scripts/extract-cyber-quizzes.js will not seed a question that puts a CED
citation in front of a student, and the refusal is all-or-nothing per quiz.
Five stems, on 2.3 and 4.1, hold back eleven questions.
Four of the five are deletions that change nothing the question asks. The
fifth is a real edit: q6 on 4.1 asked which CIA principle the CED associates
with a worm. Trimming the words would silently turn a question about the
framework into a question about reasoning, so it is replaced, and the key was
CHECKED against the four options rather than assumed. C, 'Worm, most directly
tied to Availability', still stands: a worm degrading a network most directly
threatens availability, and D shares Availability but names a logic bomb,
which does not self-replicate, so the malware-type half still discriminates.
The third held-back page, ap-cyber-unit-3-lesson-6-quiz, is NOT in this sheet
and is not fixed by it. It carries ten questions against a six-item web-quiz
ceiling, which is a bundle-instrument signal, and that is a question for a

checks.name: the generator's six assertions pass against both live bodies
checks._why: Assertion 6 is the one that matters: it runs the extractor itself against the edited bodies and requires it to ACCEPT both quizzes. A sheet that cleaned the stems and still tripped some other refusal would pass every other check here.
checks.expect: extractor accepts 2.3: 5 questions, 0 citations in any stem

checks.name: both sheets clear the Matrixify preflight
checks._why: The preflight is the gate between authored content and a live page body, and it is the one that reads mojibake through lib/mojibake.js. --carrying supplies the originals so an emoji already on the page is not read as one this sheet introduced.

checks.name: M1: 1 anchor occurs exactly once
checks._why: An anchor that matches nothing must refuse rather than write a sheet that silently skips one stem. The refusal is the whole reason anchors are read off the live page rather than retyped.

checks.name: M2: 1 staleness, replacement already live
checks._why: A sheet whose defect is already gone must not import over a page somebody else has since fixed. On 2026-09-08 a stale sheet nearly reverted a better fix by another session, which is why this rule exists at all.
checks.expect_failure: replacement is ALREADY in the live body

checks.name: M3: 2 the edit stays inside the anchored spans
checks._why: Assertion 2 is what makes the edit surgical. The FIRST version of this mutation corrupted the body after the assertions had already run, so it survived and tested nothing; it has to happen before the probe.
checks.find: //  2. the change is exactly the five spans and nothing else
checks.replace:
after = after.replace('Question 1 of', 'Questiox 1 of');
    //  2. the change is exactly the five spans and nothing else
checks.expect_failure: touched bytes outside the anchored spans

checks.name: M4: 4 no answer or explanation moved
checks._why: THE ONE THAT MATTERS. A sheet that can move an answer or an explanation is a sheet that can silently rescore a live quiz. This mutation points an anchor at text inside a checkMCQ explanation, which reverses cleanly and so passes assertion 2.
checks.find:
q: 'q3',
    find: 'with a valid CED defense',
    put: 'with a valid defense',
checks.replace:
q: 'q3',
    find: 'A, B, and C are correct CED vector-defense pairings',
    put: 'A, B, and C are correct vector-defense pairings',

checks.name: M5: 5 div balance
checks._why: Reachable only once the mutation avoids assertion 1 (a non-unique anchor) and the staleness rule (a tail trim, which makes put a substring of find). Both earlier versions tripped one of those and left div balance untested.
checks.find:
q: 'w4',
    find: 'ranked wrongly under EK 2.3.B.8, which prioritizes mitigations by',
    put: 'ranked wrongly: mitigations are prioritized by',
checks.replace: q: 'w4', find: 'class="exhero-badge">Unit 2 • 2.3 • Quiz', put: 'class="exhero-badge">Unit 2 quiz, badge',

checks.name: M6: 6 the extractor accepts both quizzes afterwards
checks._why: The rule the sheet EXISTS for. This leaves a citation in the stem in a form the staleness rule does not catch, and requires the extractor itself to refuse. A sheet that edited bytes and achieved nothing passes every other check here.
checks.find:
q: 'q5',
    find: 'Using the CED High/Moderate/Low',
    put: 'Using the High/Moderate/Low',
checks.replace:
q: 'q5',
    find: 'Using the CED High/Moderate/Low',
    put: 'Using the CED-published High/Moderate/Low',
checks.expect_failure: the extractor still refuses after the edit

checks.name: after the import, the extractor accepts 2.3 and 4.1 off the LIVE pages
checks._why: Both refuse today, so this cannot pass before the import and cannot pass if only one sheet lands. It asserts the thing the change was FOR, not that the pages were touched: a sheet that edited the bytes and left some other citation behind would still fail here.
checks.command: node -e "const sf=require('./lib/storefront-fetch');const fs=require('fs');const os=require('os');const path=require('path');const d=fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(),'live-'));for(const h of ['ap-cyber-unit-2-lesson-3-quiz','ap-cyber-unit-4-lesson-1-quiz'])fs.writeFileSync(path.join(d,h+'.html'),sf.pageBody(h).body_html);const ex=require('./scripts/extract-cyber-quizzes.js');const q=ex.extract(d);console.log('accepted='+q.length+'/2 problems='+ex.problems.length+' questions='+q.reduce((n,x)=>n+x.questions.length,0));"
